title: Levers and buttons take effect one redstone tick later
explanation: In Minecraft, flipping a lever or pressing a button powers the dust beside it at once. In Mineclonia the change is picked up on the next redstone tick (up to 0.1 s later). Everything downstream then runs with the same delays in both games, so this shifts when a circuit starts reacting to a person, not what it computes.

title: Redstone lamps light one tick later
explanation: A lamp lights in the same tick it is powered in Minecraft, and one redstone tick later in Mineclonia. Both games turn a lamp off two ticks after it loses power. Lamps are outputs only, so this affects what a display looks like for a tenth of a second, not any signal.

title: Comparator reading a container through a solid block that is itself powered at 15
explanation: A comparator can read a container through one solid block. If that block is also powered at full strength (15), Minecraft Java outputs 15 and ignores the container; Mineclonia keeps outputting the container's level. With the block unpowered, or powered below 15, both games output the container's level. Avoid powering the block between a container and its comparator.

title: Dust next to a lever or button can start powering a lamp beside it
explanation: Mineclonia connects redstone dust to lamps (and droppers and dispensers); Minecraft Java does not. craftpipe places dust with the connections Minecraft saved, so a wire running past a lamp does not light it. But using a lever or button makes Mineclonia re-shape the dust directly beside that lever or button by its own rules: if that dust also touches a lamp it was not pointing at, it connects to the lamp and lights it. The converter warns, with positions, when a build contains this arrangement. Keep one block of dust between a lever or button and any lamp the wire should pass without lighting.
